playbook:
When asked to hide at the start of a patrol, pick a central cell (4–6) to maximize initial coverage and hit probability.

On later hides, vary deliberately: if early center shots repeatedly miss, move to a low-probability corner (1–3 or 7–9) to break predictability, but do not oscillate predictably between the same two cells.

Post short, neutral, non-informative station notes: one sentence signaling readiness that reveals nothing about my hide or intent.

Follow the standing order to fire at the next live station (Echo->Foxtrot->Gamma->Echo) by default; only deviate if I have a clear tactical reason supported by observed information (e.g., I have reliable evidence someone is targeting me and a different shot would score or deter).

When I fire, choose a cell consistent with my recent hides but avoid repeating the exact same fire cell round after round if those repeats have yielded misses — vary within the same neighborhood (center/mid/corner) to probe different cells while maintaining coherence with my hiding pattern.

Never fire on Harbor (the jettison penalty makes it not worth provoking Harbor).

When the office privately tells me the true result of my shot, file the matching public claim honestly (truthful claims only).

When recording escort/salvage claims, name another live boat only if I reasonably expect reciprocity; do not claim escorts unilaterally unless there is a negotiated benefit. If no reciprocal expectation, file [salvage: none].

If I score a hit, persist with the approach that produced it for one additional round (it indicates a correct pattern), then vary slightly to avoid becoming predictable.

If opponents’ patterns emerge (e.g., repeated hits against a particular station), use that to infer their aiming habits and exploit by hiding/aiming where their shots are unlikely to go.

Avoid committing in notes to future escort reciprocity or other obligations; keep communications functional rather than strategic unless I have an explicit alliance.

When in doubt about where others are hiding, default to center for the first shot of a new pattern, then sweep outward in subsequent shots rather than re-aiming the exact same coordinate.

Always validate that any named escort is a live boat and that my claimed hits/misses match the private result before filing.

1.text:
When given a hide choice, I vary my cell; avoid always hiding in the obvious center (do not default to 5 every round). Use corners and off-center cells when I have recently been targeted by a specific opponent.

When I have been targeted recently by a specific opponent, I move off the spots they used most recently and bias hides away from their likely search pattern for at least one round.

When posting a station note, keep it non-committal and uninformative (short status, no coordinates or intentions) unless I have an explicit, confirmed deal to coordinate escorts or mutual points. Use notes only to confirm explicit escort agreements when I intend to follow through.

When the standing order tells me which station to fire at, I fire at that named boat unless there is a tactical reason not to (see Harbor rule). Follow the picket order by default to avoid breaking discipline unless a clear advantage justifies deviation.

When choosing a firing cell, randomize within a constrained set and avoid reusing the same cell repeatedly; prefer spreading shots across plausible hidden cells rather than a fixed pattern.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I file the claim exactly as required (claim must equal private result) — never invent or invert claims.

When considering escort claims, do not claim an escort unless I have a clear mutual, explicit agreement with another boat; only claim an escort if I expect the other boat to name me as well (mutual naming yields 5 points each). Set and confirm escort deals in notes within the same round before claiming.

When Harbor is the target, do not fire on Harbor unless the immediate gain is worth guaranteed political/retaliatory cost; treat Harbor as effectively off-limits by default.

When I score a hit on another boat, I expect their behavior to change (retaliation or hiding change) and immediately adjust my hide and firing pattern next round. Treat a successful hit as a trigger to increase unpredictability and to anticipate targeted counters.

When I am repeatedly missed by everyone, do not assume safety — vary hiding and firing to try to generate hits rather than staying passive. Increasing variability can create opportunities to catch a target.

When coordinating for mutual escort points, state the agreement clearly in notes and confirm reciprocity before filing salvage; if the other party does not reciprocate, do not persist in unilateral claims.

When I feel pressured or singled out, prioritize evasive hiding over aggressive, repeatable firing choices for at least one round to break the attacker’s targeting pattern.

When a choice clearly failed previously (being predictably central or firing the same cell every round), stop that behavior and adopt variability. Specifically: after being targeted twice or more, switch to a corner or opposite side for at least one turn.

Revise firing behavior if patterns emerge from observed hits and misses: if my standing-order target is consistently evasive and unrewarding, consider small deviations only when the tactical upside is clear and the picket discipline cost is low.

Do not trust perceived “steady” notes as information; treat them as neutral unless accompanied by explicit, verifiable commitments.

2.text:
When told to hide at the start of a round, pick a central cell (4–6) in early rounds to balance chance of being shot and potential to hit others.

When I am shot in a previous round, change my hide to a cell not used by me recently (do not repeat the same hide twice in a row).

When selecting a hide late in the patrol (final one or two rounds), shift toward edges (1–3 or 7–9) to reduce predictability after earlier central hides.

When posting my station note, keep it neutral and non-informative — use the team-standard phrase (for example, steady on station) unless I am explicitly setting up a mutual escort agreement.

When the standing order says to fire at the next live station, follow the standing order and target that boat.

When choosing a firing cell under the standing order, vary the numeric offset each round (don’t fire the same cell repeatedly); mix central and edge numbers so my pattern is hard to exploit. I will bias central numbers early and introduce edge numbers later.

When the office privately tells me the true shot result, file the required public claim truthfully (claim hit if told hit, claim miss if told miss).

When considering escort (salvage) claims, do not claim an escort unless I reasonably expect mutual naming; only claim an escort when I have reason to believe the named boat will name me back (mutual naming yields +5 each).

When I cannot secure a mutual escort, file salvage none rather than make a solitary escort claim for no return.

When Harbor is in play, avoid firing on Harbor unless I accept the guaranteed jettison payoff and want to remove Harbor; do not shoot Harbor routinely because it creates major negative consequences from Harbor’s standing signal.

When coordinating or attempting deals, use station notes conservatively and only to set up explicit mutual escort agreements; do not reveal hide coordinates or shot intentions in notes.

When a targeted boat has been hit previously, prefer varying my shot choices rather than repeating a prior successful cell; avoid relying on a single repeatable index to hit again because opponents observe patterns.

Do not repeat the exact phrasing of my note in quotes unless I intend to signal continuity; short, identical neutral notes are acceptable but may be used by others to infer pattern—use them only when not attempting explicit coordination.

Prioritize consistent truthful claims and low-information notes over risky signaling that could expose my hide or enable others to exploit my pattern.

Maintain the above while adjusting hide and fire choices round-to-round to avoid obvious repetition: central early, edges late; vary firing cell each round; only commit to escorts when mutuality is likely.
